headline: OpenAI President admits ChatGPT desktop app is 'a mess', teases tab-free design & new AI devices
summary: OpenAI President Greg Brockman acknowledged issues with the current ChatGPT desktop app, hinting at a future tab-free interface and plans for a range of dedicated AI devices.
details: OpenAI President Greg Brockman recently addressed the state of the ChatGPT desktop application, candidly admitting that its current iteration is 'kind of a mess'. This acknowledgement comes amidst user feedback regarding the app's functionality and design.

Brockman also hinted at upcoming improvements, specifically mentioning plans for a streamlined, tab-free interface. This redesign aims to enhance user experience and make interactions with the AI more intuitive.

Beyond software updates, Brockman revealed that OpenAI is actively 'building a family of devices' specifically for its AI chatbots. This suggests a strategic move towards integrating AI directly into hardware, expanding beyond traditional software applications.

The move into dedicated hardware could signify OpenAI's ambition to create more seamless and pervasive AI experiences. It positions the company to potentially compete in a broader consumer electronics market, driven by AI-first devices.
caption:
OpenAI's President calls the ChatGPT desktop app "a mess". Get ready for a tab-free redesign and a whole new "family of devices" for AI chatbots.

OpenAI President Greg Brockman recently addressed the state of the ChatGPT desktop application, candidly admitting that its current iteration is 'kind of a mess'. This acknowledgement comes amidst user feedback regarding the app's functionality and design.

Brockman also hinted at upcoming improvements, specifically mentioning plans for a streamlined, tab-free interface. This redesign aims to enhance user experience and make interactions with the AI more intuitive.

Beyond software updates, Brockman revealed that OpenAI is actively 'building a family of devices' specifically for its AI chatbots. This suggests a strategic move towards integrating AI directly into hardware, expanding beyond traditional software applications.

The move into dedicated hardware could signify OpenAI's ambition to create more seamless and pervasive AI experiences. It positions the company to potentially compete in a broader consumer electronics market, driven by AI-first devices.
